_about: Hand-made grouping of every property that passed discovery on TRAIN authors (BH q < 0.05) into named drivers. Grouping is by meaning only; whether a property replicated on test authors was not used, so the scorecard's test score stays honest. kind: write = a writing choice the author can make in this post; occasion = only if it is true (something real has to have happened); descr = describes the post, not advice.

people.name: Real people
people.summary: Name, thank and credit the actual people involved.
people.advice: Say who was involved and what they did. Replace "thanks to the team" with names. If someone helped you get here, credit them.
members: Credit specific people for helping you reach something
Thank a specific person or group
Express thanks, sympathy or good wishes
Give a shout-out to a person or team
Say what you learned from a specific person
Tell a client's or founder's story
Show support for a specific group of people

moments.name: Your own news and real moments
moments.summary: Something that actually happened to you: a milestone, an event, a result.
moments.advice: When you have news, post it. Frame other posts around what actually happened: where you were, what you finished, what comes next.
members: Announce a milestone in your own career
Describe a turning point in your career or life
Describe an event you took part in
Announce that you are taking part in something
Report on something that just finished
Say you are proud of something
Say what you are excited about next
Say how long you have been at it
Report a number you or your team achieved
Show how your work happens behind the scenes

voice.name: Personal voice
voice.summary: Write as a person: your experience, your feelings, your mistakes.
voice.advice: Anchor the post in something you lived through and say how it felt. A doubt, a mistake or a joke at your own expense works better than a polished brand voice.
members: Include a specific experience of your own
Make a joke at your own expense
Share a lesson you learned first-hand
Tell it as a story (a sequence of events)
State your own background or experience
Write in the first person (I, my)
State your opinion as your own ("I think")
Speak from your own role ("as a founder")
Use a vivid image (colour, weather, temperature)

concrete.name: Concrete details
concrete.summary: Places, names, numbers and examples instead of general statements.
concrete.advice: Swap general statements for specifics: the city, the company, the number, the date, what happened first.
members: Open in a specific moment (time, place, action)
Open with a named person, company or product
Put a number in the first line
Mention your own project or work

company_news.name: Company and market news
company_news.summary: Funding, launches, hiring and other recent developments.
company_news.advice: Report the development plainly: who, what, how much.
members: Mention a specific amount of money
Give a named company's measured result
Report a recent company update or release
Discuss hiring or the job market
Highlight someone giving free help or charity

rhetoric.name: Contrast and analogy
rhetoric.summary: Explains by comparing two things or using a metaphor.
rhetoric.advice: A contrast or an analogy helps a little. It does not make up for missing people or experience.
members: Use a "not X, but Y" contrast

marks.name: Hashtags, emoji and emphasis
marks.summary: Surface marks: hashtags, emoji, exclamation marks, capitals.
marks.advice: These go with more reactions on train authors, but hashtags did not hold up on held-out authors. Do not rely on them.
members: Use an emoji in the body

lists.name: Lists
lists.summary: Items set out as a list.
lists.advice: A list is fine and slightly helps reposts. It is not a substitute for content.
members: Include a list of three or more items

lecture.name: Lecture mode
lecture.summary: Advice, frameworks and made-up examples with nothing of your own behind them.
lecture.advice: If you give advice, tie it to something that happened to you or to a named person. Replace "imagine a company that..." with a real case.
members: Advice not tied to anything you experienced
Tips or recommended actions for the reader
A step-by-step roadmap for the reader
Argues for a specific method or technology
A made-up example not tied to a real case

problems.name: Problem and risk framing
problems.summary: The post is built around a problem, a gap or a risk.
problems.advice: Problem posts draw comments more than reactions. If reactions matter, lead with what you or someone did about it.
members: Points out a problem, gap or risk
Describes a difficulty a group of people has
Describes a limitation or risk of a technology

hooks.name: Hook-style openers
hooks.summary: Opens with a bold claim, a contradiction or a question.
hooks.advice: Open with what happened or who it is about, not with a claim, a "everyone is wrong" line or a question.
members: Opens with a bold one-line claim
Opens with a contradiction ("Everyone says X. They're wrong.")

elsewhere.name: Sends readers elsewhere
elsewhere.summary: Links out, or summarises someone else's article.
elsewhere.advice: Say the point in the post itself. If a link is needed, make the post worth reading without clicking it.
members: Points the reader to an external resource

layout.name: No paragraph breaks
layout.summary: The post is one block of text.
layout.advice: Break the post into paragraphs. One block of text loses reactions even at the same length.
members: One block of text with no paragraph breaks

asks.name: Asks the reader
asks.summary: Asks the reader a question or to reply with a keyword.
asks.advice: Questions raise comments a little and lower reactions a little. "Reply with a number or keyword" clearly lowers reactions.
members: Asks the reader a direct question
Asks readers to reply with a keyword or number
